If Voat gets popular enough, it may eventually face the same issues as reddit in terms of becoming more profitable to advertisers and such. Alternative: some form of pay system. There are many options for something like this.

  • 1-time fee, like how the SomethingAwful forums (used to?) operate per username
  • monthly/yearly subscription (removes upvote/downvote/submission caps, other bennies)
  • Voat Aluminum (goats don't eat gold)
  • paid hats, flairs, site skins, etc. like popular Free-to-Play games such as League of Legends, TeamFortress 2, or Dota2 (I want a unicorn goat avatar)

Just a couple ideas off the top of my head. There are lots more options. Of course, the whole idea of paying money to support voat has ups and downs.

Pros

  • some pay forms (subscriptions, one-time fee, etc) keeps out shitposters
  • funds site directly
  • paying actual $$ increases feeling of ownership in site, could boost participation
  • revenue sharing with popular subs and posters to encourage OC (gifmakers, dank memers, indie artists, game makers, etc.)

Cons

  • cost could prohibit some people from joining and shrink userbase
  • paywalls would suck (please don't)
  • advertising revenue gets lurkers (but a subscription could turn off ads! Problem solved!)
  • giving personal $$ info to site is risky, esp. since voat is a target

Personally, I'd like to see a one-time fee for registering a username of either $5 to Voat or $10 to a charity of choice.

If Wikipedia, the 7th most trafficked site on the web, can run ad-free and donation-only, then Voat could too. A pledge drive now and then wouldn't be too irksome, and donors wouldn't have as much clout to demand changes to the creators vision as corporate marketers would.
